name: NGC 4490, NGC4490-2011OT1 field (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 4490, an interacting galaxy that hosted the luminous red nova NGC4490-2011OT1, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc4490ot-hubble
story: This outburst in NGC 4490 was first taken for a supernova impostor and is now counted among the luminous red novae, flares that astronomers think most likely come from a close pair of stars ejecting a shared envelope. NGC 4490 itself is tangled with its neighbor NGC 4485 in the pair known as Arp 260.

claims.text: NGC4490-2011OT1, also known as PSN J12304185+4137498, is a luminous red nova
It was first classified as an SN impostor
Common envelope ejection in a close binary is favored as the most likely explanation for luminous red novae
Host NGC 4490 is a barred spiral (SBcd) in an interacting pair with NGC 4485 known as Arp 260
